facts.raw_span: subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts
subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

concepts.why: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions, a high white blood cell count, and a cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts support the diagnosis of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions and restriction of diffusion in the cutaneous scalp support the diagnosis of Leukemia Cutis.
The presence of severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots support the diagnosis of Neurolymphomatosis.
The presence of severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes support the diagnosis of Guillain-Barré Syndrome.
The presence of severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes support the diagnosis of Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy.
The presence of a high white blood cell count and a high red blood cell count support the diagnosis of Multiple Myeloma.
The presence of a high white blood cell count and a cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts support the diagnosis of Waldenström's Macroglobulinemia.
The presence of severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes support the diagnosis of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.

rationales.F01: Subacute progressive symmetric lower extremity weakness is more typical of leukemia or lymphoma than other conditions.
rationales.F04: Severe flaccid quadriparesis is a strong indicator of a severe neurological condition such as leukemia or lymphoma.
rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are highly suggestive of leukemia cutis.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is indicative of neurolymphomatosis or leukemia.
rationales.F10: A high white blood cell count with a predominance of atypical cells/blasts is highly suggestive of leukemia.
rationales.F11: A cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts is diagnostic of leukemia.
